sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a straight line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales for the year [P72].
Revenue then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 to $44.0 billion [F6][D231] and 16.5% in FY2023 to $61.3 billion [F8][D322], before falling 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [F9][F10][D367][D412].
The FY2024 decline came as rising global grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates cut shipment volumes [P17].
Production Agriculture was the largest product line at 37.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D657], and it fell 17.6%, subtracting 7.0pp from revenue growth [D658][D659].
In FY2025 Production & Precision Agriculture sales volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Construction & Forestry was 25.5% of revenue and fell 11.8% in FY2025 [D889][D890], while Financial Services grew to 13.8% of revenue [D922].
Operating income compounded 16.9% a year to FY2024 against revenue's 6.2% to FY2025 [F159][F157], and EPS grew 16.1% against net income's 14.2% [F161][F160].
Diluted shares fell from 316.6 million in FY2016 to 271.7 million in FY2025 [X110][X119], so per-share growth outran net income.
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1335][D1334].
The FY2024 margin fell 3.7pp [D378], with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D391][D390], as revenue fell faster than operating costs by 3.7pp [D389].
In FY2025 net margin fell 2.7pp to 11.0% [F50][D422], and net margin sat 3.7pp below operating margin in FY2024 [D1373].
Interest expense reached $3.17 billion in FY2025 [X82], and the effective tax rate was 20.1% [D400].
Small Agriculture & Turf operating profit fell on lower sales volumes and higher tariffs, partly offset by price realization [P8].
Operating cash flow was $7.46 billion and free cash flow $6.10 billion in FY2025 [F80][F100], a 13.4% free-cash-flow margin [D398].
Free cash flow was 1.21x net income in FY2025 against a 0.91x window median [D402][D1347], and the 13.4% margin was near the 11.6% median [D398][D1341].
Capex was $1.36 billion, 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [F90][D397][D403].
FY2025 operating cash flow was driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Cash was $8.28 billion at FY2025 [F140], up 13.0% [D420], against $13.8 billion of current debt [X185].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021 [X191], so net cash and debt-based peer ranks cannot be computed across the window [R9].
Buybacks plus dividends were $2.86 billion in FY2025, 46.9% of free cash flow [D409][D410], with $1.14 billion of repurchases and $1.72 billion of dividends [X129][X139].
Return on average equity was 20.6% in FY2025 [D411], below the 28.3% industrials peer median [D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [F9][F10], a two-year decline [R1].
Production Agriculture, 37% of revenue, fell 18% in FY2025 [D657][D658][R2], and Construction & Forestry, 25% of revenue, fell 12% [D889][D890][R4].
Long-term debt is missing after FY2021 [X191], so net cash and debt growth are omitted across the break [R9].
The FY2017 SG&A figure was later restated to $3,098.0 million from $3,066.6 million [X34][R8], a data-quality item that does not change the conclusions.
Watch whether FY2026 revenue holds above the FY2025 level of $45.7 billion [F10], with the FY2026 10-K.
Watch whether operating margin recovers toward the 21.2% FY2023 high from 17.5% in FY2024 [F30][D1334], with the FY2026 10-K.
Watch whether free cash flow stays above the 11.6% window median margin from 13.4% in FY2025 [D398][D1341], with the FY2026 10-K.
